tool_input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(mcp): authenticate WebSocket transport, restrict origin and bind address

beadle-nimy: the ws transport had three gaps. (1) No authentication --
any client that could reach the port got full MCP access. WSServer now
generates a random bearer token at construction (Token() to retrieve
it) and HandleMCP requires it via an "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
header or a "token" query parameter, checked with a constant-time
comparison, before upgrading. (2) CheckOrigin unconditionally returned
true, accepting any cross-origin request; removed in favor of
gorilla/websocket's default, which rejects a mismatched Origin header
and allows requests with none (the case for non-browser MCP clients).
(3) ListenAndServe bound 0.0.0.0; changed to 127.0.0.1, the default for
Punt Labs daemons -- network exposure needs explicit opt-in this
server doesn't offer yet. Updated the two existing WS tests to present
the token on dial.
EOF
)"

prose: |
  Fixed all four P1 security beads with one commit per bead, all on top
  of the existing failing-test commits:

  beadle-p43a (internal/daemon/runner.go): ClaudeRunner.Run distinguished
  MCPServers == nil (field omitted -> default set) from an explicit
  MCPServers: [] (recipe opts out -> zero servers) by switching the guard
  from len(servers) == 0 to servers == nil.

  beadle-vr0v (internal/daemon/templates.go): the system prompt's
  result-submission instruction ("ethos mission result ... --file <path>")
  requires a shell. Added BuildSystemPromptForTools(missionID, tools),
  which includes that instruction only when Bash is in the declared tool
  set (or the set is nil, meaning default/full). BuildSystemPrompt kept
  its original one-arg signature and full-instruction behavior for
  existing callers/tests, delegating to the new function with tools=nil
  -- this avoided touching templates_test.go, which sits outside the
  mission's write set and calls the old signature. runner.go's call site
  now passes cmd.Tools through the new function.

  beadle-hv7i (internal/daemon/handler.go): verifyTrust passed through
  channel.Trusted purely from the message's own TrustLevel, without
  checking that the IMAP source is actually loopback (where Proton
  Bridge, not an arbitrary server, controls the X-Pm-* headers). Added
  isLoopbackHost(host string) using net.SplitHostPort plus a
  127.0.0.1/::1/localhost check; a Trusted classification against a
  non-loopback IMAP host now downgrades to Unverified with a logged
  warning.

  beadle-nimy (internal/mcp/ws.go, ws_test.go): three gaps in the
  WebSocket transport. (1) No authentication -- added a random 256-bit
  hex bearer token generated in NewWSServer (via crypto/rand), exposed
  through Token(), and required by HandleMCP via an "Authorization:
  Bearer <token>" header or a "token" query parameter, compared with
  crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare; a missing/wrong token gets a 401
  before the WebSocket upgrade. (2) CheckOrigin unconditionally returned
  true; removed the override so gorilla/websocket's default applies
  (rejects a request whose Origin doesn't match Host, allows requests
  with no Origin header -- the case for non-browser MCP/CLI clients).
  (3) ListenAndServe bound 0.0.0.0; changed to 127.0.0.1, the Punt Labs
  daemon default. Updated the two pre-existing WS tests
  (TestWSServer_MCPInitialize, TestWSServer_ListenAndServe) to present
  the token on dial, per the mission's explicit permission to touch
  ws_test.go for this.

  Note on templates_test.go: it is not in the mission's write set but
  calls the old single-argument BuildSystemPrompt signature. Rather than
  edit it (write-set violation) or break its compilation (signature
  change), I kept BuildSystemPrompt's original signature as a thin
  wrapper over the new BuildSystemPromptForTools, so that test compiles
  and passes unchanged while runner.go calls the tools-aware variant
  directly. Flagging this in case the leader wants the wrapper collapsed
  once templates_test.go is back in a write set.

  Commit order matched the suggestion: p43a, vr0v, hv7i, nimy -- one
  commit per bead, each passing make check at commit time.
